chunks: Via his chain from Ibrahim ibn Hashim that Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr was a cloth merchant

so his wealth perished and he fell into poverty, and he had ten thousand dirhams due from a man, so the man sold his house which he used to live in for ten thousand dirhams and carried the money to his door, so Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr came out to him and said: 'What is this?' He said: 'This is your money which is due upon me.' He said: 'Did you inherit it?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Was it gifted to you?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Is it the price of a land you have sold?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then what is it?' He said: 'I sold my house in which I live so that I can repay my debt.'
So Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr said: 'Darih al-Muharibi narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: A man is not driven out of his place of residence because of debt.'
'Take it away, for I have no need of it. By Allah, even though I have a need of a single dirham at this time, I will not take a single one of them into my possession.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a debtor selling their home to pay off debts?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Al-Faqih* illustrates the practical application of Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) legal principle that debt does not compel a debtor to forfeit their primary residence, a ruling that protects the dignity and stability of the individual. Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr’s acceptance and subsequent return of the funds highlight the distinction between mere possession and true ownership, emphasizing that the house remained his asset despite the sale for debt repayment. This incident serves as a key example of how solitary reports (khabar al-wahid) from truthful narrators are utilized in Shia jurisprudence to derive specific social and financial rulings.

en.ammaar-muslim: 11. [11/-] al-Faqih: Via his chain from Ibrahim b. Hashim that:

Muhammad b. Abi Umayr was a cloth merchant whose wealth perished and he fell into poverty, however he had loaned out ten thousand silver coins to someone, so the one he owed sold his house which he used to live in at a price of ten thousand silver coins and carried the whole sum to his (Ibn Abi Umayr’s) door, so Muhammad b. Abi Umayr came out to him and said: what is this? he said: this is your money which was due upon me, he said: you have inherited it? he said: no, he said: it has been gifted to you? he said: no, he said: is it the price of a land you have sold? He said: no, he said: then what is it? he said: I sold my house in which I live in so that I can repay my debt,
so Muhammad b. Abi Umayr said: Dharih al-Muharibi narrated to me from Abi Abdillah that he said: a man is not driven out of his place of residence (his home) because of debt,
take it away for I have no need of it, by Allah even though I do have a need of even a single silver coin at this time – I will not take a single one of them into my possession.
